title: CREATE TABLE
summary: Design a table: columns, types, keys, defaults, and how databases disagree about them.

steps.title: Harbor Lights Theatre
body: Month six. Larkspur has bought **Harbor Lights**, a 1920s theatre on the waterfront. Its box office runs on a spreadsheet with forty tabs. Rosa: *"No more querying other people's mistakes. This time **you** design the database."*
```sql
CREATE TABLE shows (
id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
title   TEXT    NOT NULL,
starts  TEXT    NOT NULL,          -- '2026-12-04 19:30'
price   REAL    NOT NULL DEFAULT 25.0,
notes   TEXT                        -- may be NULL
Each column has a **name**, a **type**, and optional **constraints**:
- `PRIMARY KEY` identifies each row; it's unique and (in practice) never NULL.
- `NOT NULL` makes the value required.
- `DEFAULT` fills the value when an INSERT leaves the column out.
`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS shows;` removes a table and all its data. There's no confirmation prompt.

steps.title: The shows table
prompt: Create a table **`shows`** with exactly these columns, in this order:
steps.stateQuery: SELECT 'shows' AS t, 'col ' || name || ' ' || upper(type) || ' ' || CASE WHEN pk > 0 THEN 'pk' || pk ELSE 'nn' || "notnull" END AS d FROM pragma_table_info('shows') UNION ALL SELECT 'shows', 'fk ' || "from" || ' -> ' || "table" || '.' || COALESCE("to", '?') || ' ' || on_delete FROM pragma_foreign_key_list('shows') UNION ALL SELECT 'shows', 'unique ' || (SELECT group_concat(ii.name) FROM pragma_index_info(il.name) AS ii) FROM pragma_index_list('shows') AS il WHERE il."unique" = 1 AND il.origin <> 'pk' UNION ALL SELECT 'shows', 'check ' || (instr(upper(sql), 'CHECK') > 0) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'shows' ORDER BY 1, 2
hints: `CREATE TABLE shows ( ... );` with one line per column, separated by commas.

steps.title: Types, and how databases differ
body: Every database has types for whole numbers, decimals, text and dates, but the names differ, and so does auto-numbering:
```text
auto-numbered key                       text           exact money
SQLite        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (AUTOINCREMENT)   TEXT           INTEGER cents
PostgreSQL    id SERIAL / INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY   TEXT, VARCHAR(n)   NUMERIC(10,2)
SQL Server    id INT IDENTITY(1,1)                    NVARCHAR(n)    DECIMAL(10,2)
MySQL         id INT AUTO_INCREMENT                   VARCHAR(n)     DECIMAL(10,2)
**SQLite is unusual:** types are *affinities*, not rules. It will store `'abc'` in an `INTEGER` column. `CREATE TABLE ... STRICT` (3.37+) makes it enforce types like other databases.
> **Money:** never use floating point (`REAL`, `FLOAT`) for money. `0.1 + 0.2` is not exactly `0.3`. Store cents in an integer, or use `DECIMAL`.

code: SELECT n, typeof(n) FROM t ORDER BY rowid;
steps.explain: SQLite converts `'12'` to the integer 12 because the column prefers integers. `'abc'` can't be converted, so it's kept as text. PostgreSQL would reject the second row.

steps.prompt: A table has `price INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 2500`. Which INSERT fails?
steps.explain: An explicit NULL is not 'missing', so the DEFAULT isn't used, and NOT NULL rejects it.
